newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT - Indian statement on foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: TEXT - Indian statement on foreign investment.

text.p: Following is a statement released on Friday by the Indian government on foreign investment in infrastructure:
"Vast infrastructure is needed for the infrastructure sector which has been the special focus of the Government.

These sectors are highly capital intensive and some of them have a ceiling on total foreign equity that can be brought in a company operating in these sectors. These companies are not able to raise adequate funds in the domestic market under the approved financing pattern. Therefore, many projects are yet to take off.
In this scenario, it is imperative to find ways and means by which there can be augmentation of resources in these important infrastructure sectors.

This subject has been considered by the FIPB (Foreign Investment Promotion Board) from time to time and on its recommendations the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment (CCFI) in its meeting held on October 17 has taken some important decisions which will be issued in the form (of) guidelines of FIPB in due course.

The CCFI has decided that companies operating in the infrastructure sector may bring in equity through the mechanism of an investing company for the purpose of making investment in a licencee company in the services sector where there is a prescribed foreign equity cap such as in the telecom services sector and an investing company by virtue of its being the registered Indian company should be allowed to make investment in the licencee company and such investment should be treated as part of domestic equity.

While computing the total equity in a licencee/Indian company, only direct investment should be considered in the prescribed cap (49 percent or less) and the FDI (foreign direct investment) in an investing company should not be set off against this cap provided the FDI is less than 49 percent and the management of the investing company is with the Indian owners.
This arrangement will ensure the objective of Indian control over the licencee company while allowing the Indian promoters to augment their resources by raising funds overseas.
The character of the holding company continues to be Indian, and all its investment in its subsidiary would be in Indian rupees.
This arrangement will also enable the domestic companies which have the inherent strength of raising finance to start up operations of their business."
